name: edge_bevel_offset_law
description: Task 1150 measured it, task 1170 ported it -- divergence-ledger row 1, the edge-bevel offset law, settled on 53 cells / 520 created vertices to a residual of 1.53e-5 x inset. Two rules and no face normal: SLIDE puts a new vertex at v + inset*unit(e) on every un-bevelled edge at a touched vertex; MITER puts one in the PLANE OF THE TWO BEVELLED EDGES at perpendicular distance `inset` from both lines, with a whole-ring normal deciding only which of the two such points is the inward one. All 53 cells declare an EMPTY gap. That is parity, and runKnownDivergenceSuite asserts an empty gap exactly as strictly as a full one -- an extra or a lost vertex on any of them is a failure. The case names keep the measured split because it is a property of the cells, not of our current state: 31 `slide_and_miter/` cells carry the 117 mitred corners that exercise the in-face question, 22 `slide_only/` cells carry none and could not arbitrate it. A mitre regression reddens in the first group and is invisible in the second. No cell here is a cube: on a closed solid every candidate rule agrees and the matrix would decide nothing.
source: Reference side: the frozen 53-cell behavioural matrix in toolcards/edge_bevel_offset_normal (106 headless boots, ring rotations included so a ring-order-dependent normal is refuted rather than assumed away). Our side: read live off vibe3d at generation time through the same HTTP steps the test replays.

provenance.harness: tools/local/dogfood/bevnorm (the 53-cell matrix) placed into tests/ by tools/local/fixture_gen/ring_order (task 1150)
provenance.notes: The law was settled by TWO instruments: a static read of the shipped binaries that named every normal the bevel code touches, and the 53-cell behavioural matrix that then REFUTED the candidate that read predicted. Ring rotation is what killed it: the measurement does not move when the ring start does. Bevelled edges are keyed by coordinate pair here; the toolcard keys them by index. The vibe3d side was re-read live after task 1170 ported the mitre to `math.bevelMiterPoint`; the reference side is the same frozen matrix as before the port and was not re-measured.
